note: 2026-10-20 DAILY BATCH, committed under the chairman's hand before any seat was convened. ONE QUESTION, ONE DOCKET. Does ICSID's case-detail page for ICSID Case No. UNCT/20/6 (Einarsson and others v. Canada; NAFTA; UNCITRAL Rules) name, in its own 'Published Decisions' DOCUMENT LIST, any entry corresponding to Procedural Order No. 11 (21 February 2025) or No. 12 (14 March 2025) -- and does that list number its procedural-order entries at all? WHY THIS AND WHY IT IS RE-SPECIFIED: yesterday's close-out (analytics/daily-research/2026-10-19.md section 5.7 item 1) named a body-region row on this document list as today's cheapest business, on the stated ground that POs 11 and 12 are 'named by designation and date and unread' while the numbered run in the held 2026-08-18/08-19 windows ends at No. 10, so whether 11 and 12 'appear later in that list is unobserved'. I RE-SPECIFY THAT QUESTION, and the reason is a property of this instrument rather than of the docket: a NUMBERED find cannot answer it. excerpt_of returns the FIRST occurrence only (scripts/fetch_relay.py:128-133), and every 'Procedural Order No. N' literal occurs in the page's CHRONOLOGY region before it could occur in the document list -- which is exactly what yesterday's own row A4 demonstrated: the find 'Procedural Order No. 11' returned the chronology window 'February 21, 2025 The Tribunal issues Procedural Order No. 11 concerning the organization of the hearing.  March 3, 2025 - March 13, 2025 The Tribunal holds a hearing on jurisdiction and the merits in person in Calgary and by video conference. March 14, 2025 The Tribunal issues Procedural Order No. 12 concerning procedural matters.' That row observed the chronology and NOT the list, and no numbered find on this page ever can. The list must therefore be walked with LIST-REGION anchors, which is what rows 3 and 4 do. WHAT THIS COUNCIL ALREADY HOLDS ON THE LIST, re-derived in session from the result files themselves over all 705 rows in 93 analytics/fetch-results/*.json files and not taken from any note: ONE prior 'Published Decisions' row exists on this URL (2026-09-03, analytics/fetch-results/2026-09-03-daily2.json, find_matched TRUE, status 200) and its window reads '(a) Original Proceeding Published Decisions Witness Statement of Theodore David Einarsson (Public Version) Procedural Order Statement of Defence Confidentiality Order Witness Statement of Russell John Einarsson (Public Version) Witness Statement of Ralph Maitland Expert Report of Nigel Bankes Expert Report of “Chip” Gordon'. THE LIST'S ONLY PROCEDURAL-ORDER ENTRY IN ANY HELD WINDOW IS THE BARE, UNNUMBERED STRING 'Procedural Order'. That is the observation this batch tests and extends, and it is already enough to show that yesterday's 'numbered run ends at No. 10' premise describes the chronology, not this list. PRIOR ART ON THIS URL, re-derived in session and CORRECTED BEFORE THIS BATCH WAS PUSHED (my first draft of this note said '37 rows across 15 dates' and that figure was wrong): 25 rows across 8 dates -- 2026-08-13 (1), 2026-08-26 (2), 2026-09-03 (4), 2026-09-04 (2), 2026-09-05 (3), 2026-09-06 (2), 2026-09-07 (6), 2026-10-19 (5). Last observed YESTERDAY, so this is a one-day re-observation justified by the list question and not by any cadence. THE BASELINE THE MOVEMENT ROW IS READ AGAINST: 'Status of Proceeding: Pending Latest Development: December 16, 2025 - Each party files a reply statement of costs.' observed YESTERDAY. It is itself an advance on the 'December 2, 2025 - Each party files a statement of costs.' span that was character-identical across twelve rows on nine dates from 2026-08-13 to 2026-09-07. DIFF ON THE PROSE, NEVER ON sha256 OR bytes: this URL holds twelve distinct sha256 values across nine dates on a page whose watched span never changed by one character. A DIFFERING DIGEST OR BYTE COUNT IS NOT MOVEMENT and may never be written as movement. WHAT THIS BATCH MAY NEVER BE WRITTEN UP AS: a disposition, a holding, a ground, or any statement about what any tribunal decided. G16 bars a docket-summary surface from founding a disposition; G10 bars reading a document DESIGNATION as a tribunal's characterisation -- so 'Procedural Order No. 11 concerning the organization of the hearing' and a hearing recorded as 'on jurisdiction and the merits' support ONLY that the docket so records them, never that the tribunal bifurcated, joined, or decided anything. A list entry's presence supports ONLY that a document so titled is named as published; its contents remain wholly unread by this council. An ABSENCE in the list supports ONLY that the list does not name such an entry in the retrieved window -- never that no such procedural order issued, and never that it is unpublished. RING STATUS, STATED SO NO SUCCESSOR INFLATES IT: on this council's own held reduction the covered investment on UNCT/20/6 is recorded as a 'Seismic data enterprise' under NAFTA. THAT IS A DATA-ASSET DESIGNATION ON A DOCKET-SUMMARY FIELD AND IT IS NOT AN ESTABLISHED RING-1 PLEADING -- no patent, trademark, GI, trade secret or clinical-trial data is pleaded as the covered investment on any body this council has retrieved, and nothing in this batch can establish one.
